Kill the ~73k-launch storm on the dominant batch=640 n=512 (and batch=60 n=1024) cases with a one-CTA-per-matrix blocked Householder Triton kernel: each program factors one matrix, staging only nb-column panels (e.g. nb=32 -> 512x32=64KB) in shared memory while the trailing matrix stays in HBM; compute the nb reflectors in-panel, build a WY block reflector, and apply the trailing update with tensor-core tl.dot. 640 matrices become 640 concurrent CTAs in a single launch. Emit exact geqrf-compact (H,tau).

Iteration 1+2: one-CTA-per-matrix blocked Householder Triton kernel (panel register-resident, FP32 trailing WY update tiled over rows/cols with tensor-core tl.dot), off-grid/large-n-low-batch route to geqrf. Iter1 geomean 7956.10us (14.56x). Iter2 per-shape tile tuning -> 7458.93us (15.53x). Validates clean incl all 3 guards.

Fuse panel inner-loop into ONE [NRP,NB] rewrite per reflector (drop redundant col re-extraction), cutting register-spill traffic that dominated the bandwidth-bound (92% DRAM, ncu Est. Local Speedup 95.81%) kernel. n=512 15051->12127us, n=1024 20123->17186us. Geomean 6477.10us (17.88x). Validates clean.

BEST: geomean 6477.10us = 17.88x vs baseline 115819.775us (commit 3a979fb3). One-CTA-per-matrix blocked Householder Triton kernel: each program factors one matrix, panel (NRP-padded n x NB) factored register-resident, trailing WY update C-=V(T^T(V^T C)) row/col-tiled with FP32 tensor-core tl.dot. Off-grid/tiny/large-n-low-batch route to torch.geqrf (also the board-confirmed off-grid-n fix). Validates clean incl all 3 guards (diff-correctness, invariance to B=1280, off-grid-n). Per-shape: n=512 ~12127us (79x), n=1024 ~17186us (13x), n=176 345us(45x), n=352 1357us(28x), n=32 27us(10x). WORKED: (1) collapsing 73k launches->1 launch is the dominant win; (2) FUSING the panel inner loop to ONE [NRP,NB] rewrite/reflector cut register-spill traffic, 15051->12127us at n=512 (+15% geomean); (3) per-shape tile tuning. DIDN'T WORK / dead ends: TF32 tl.dot fails ill-conditioned gates (rankdef/clustered/mixed) AND is useless since kernel is COMPUTE-idle (5.8% SM); V-resident trailing (no row-tiling) OOMs shared (Blackwell RTX PRO 6000 has only 100KB/SM, NOT 228KB); recursive 2-level panel (SB=16 sub-panels) no net gain; maxnreg>38 HURTS (kills the occupancy that hides spills); larger NB(64) catastrophic panel spill; num_stages/larger-BN neutral. ROOT BOTTLENECK: kernel is MEMORY-BANDWIDTH-BOUND at 92% / 1.47TB/s (ncu); panel working-set (n*NB floats) cannot fit registers at bandwidth-saturating occupancy so it spills to local mem (HBM), and trailing re-reads V across column-tiles -- both fundamental to one-CTA-per-matrix at these dims in Triton (no slicing of resident tensors; 100KB shared ceiling). CEILING: the two geqrf-fallback shapes n=2048(72ms) & n=4096(54ms) are now the LARGEST per-shape values and cap the geomean at ratio~1; one-CTA-per-matrix fundamentally starves the SMs at batch=8/2 (measured 0.35x/0.01x vs geqrf). SUGGEST NEXT: (a) worker-2's cooperative/multi-CTA-per-matrix is the only path for n=2048/4096; combining my n<=1024 kernel with a cooperative large-n kernel would lift the geomean most. (b) A within-panel column-carry that avoids the per-step full-panel reduction reads could cut panel spill bytes further but needs Triton tensor-slicing it lacks. (c) leaderboard submission still BLOCKED (popcorn not authed).

The n=512(x4)+n=1024(x3) regime is ~61% of the geomean log-sum and is the trailing_update bandwidth wall: blocked Householder re-reads trailing C ~n/nb times (profiled 60% time, 73% DRAM at nb=32). Attack it on the batched-panel backbone by making large nb viable: factor each nb panel via a FIXED 2-level WY blocking (outer nb, inner sub-panel sb via tl.static_range) so the panel becomes GEMM-rich (tensor-core tl.dot sub-panel updates) instead of a flat O(nb) sequential loop that spills. Target nb=64 (halves C passes 16->8, ~25-30% win); nb=128 stretch with sb-striped accumulation to fit ~100KB smem. Emits exact (H,tau) -- NO reconstruction. Distinct from the prior occupancy-starved one-CTA 2-level attempt.

It DID speed up the nb=64 panel vs flat (n512 nb64: 2level 14466us vs flat 15926us) BUT nb=64 STILL LOSES to nb=32 end-to-end (n512: nb64 14466 vs nb32 10510; n1024: nb64 10477 vs nb32 8279). ROOT CAUSE (measured, isolated trailing sweep over all BM/BN/warps): the nb=64 trailing GEMM is 13% SLOWER than nb=32 (n512: 7182 vs 6370us; n1024: 5253 vs 4647us) despite halving C-passes -- the rank-64 update's X=[64,BLOCK_N] accumulator collapses occupancy below the DRAM-saturation point, so the C-read-halving is fully masked. The consultant's 'high-batch => DRAM-bound not occupancy-bound' is WRONG for this kernel: at nb=64 it becomes occupancy-bound. This independently confirms worker-1's nb=64 finding. WHAT WORKED (the real win): trailing is occupancy-limited at the DEFAULT config (worker1: 8% occ, trail_warps=4). Structured sweep found BLOCK_M=32 + trail_warps=8 lifts occupancy toward DRAM saturation: n512 (nb32,BM32,BN128,pw4,tw8) 10590->9550us, n1024 (nb32,BM32,BN64,pw8,tw8) 8307->7530us, also retuned n176 336->313, n352 872->850. DEAD ENDS (all measured): (a) trailing precision is already optimal/free -- tf32x3 ~= ieee(FP32) ~= tf32 in wall time (DRAM-bound), and tf32 FAILS the ill-cond factor gate (rankdef/clustered/mixed); register pressure from tf32x3 does NOT limit wall-time. (b) Fusing worker1's two per-reflector panel rewrites into one tl.where (my brief-0 panel win) REGRESSES here (n512 9547->9856) -- different panel (variable BLOCK_M, tf32x3, 255 regs). (c) 2-level panel at nb=32 adds row-tiled within-panel overhead -> slower than flat (11224 vs 10510). (d) C-staging across the two trailing passes / V-resident trailing hits the 100KB smem wall (full-height [512,*] dot operands overflow). ROOT BOTTLENECK (final profile n512, HEAD): trailing_update 68% (DRAM-bound, C read 2x/step is fundamental to the rank-k update; fewer C-passes needs bigger nb which kills occupancy -- no escape on sm_120) + panel_factor 23% (latency-bound, 255 regs/14.75% occ) + build_T 9%. Both at the structural floor for this algorithm on this GPU, now independently confirmed by worker-1 AND me. CEILING: geomean is dominated by n=2048 (71889us) & n=4096 (48466us), both geqrf (worker-1 brief-1 proved CholeskyQR infeasible: random large-n A has cond>>1/eps32). SUGGEST NEXT: (1) the only remaining large win is worker-2's within-matrix-parallel cooperative blocked Householder for n=2048/4096 (one-CTA/batched-panel both starve SMs at batch 8/2). (2) Small free win nobody took: n=32 still on geqrf (288us) but a one-CTA kernel does it in ~27us (10x) -- worth folding in. (3) The panel_factor 255-reg/15%-occ latency floor is the other wall; a cooperative (multi-CTA/matrix) panel could raise its occupancy but that's worker-2 territory.

Attack the trailing DRAM-bytes floor from a NEW angle: L2-cache-blocking by matrix-group. Today the loop is 'for each panel j: trailing_update over ALL 640 matrices', so between matrix-0's panel-j and panel-(j+1) the kernel streams ~639MB of other matrices' C, evicting matrix-0's 1MB C from the ~100MB L2 -> all 16 re-reads MISS to HBM. Reorder to 'matrix-GROUP x (all 16 panels for that group)', group sized so the group's trailing C fits L2 (n=512: ~64 matrices x1MB=64MB; n=1024: ~16x4MB=64MB). Inter-trailing panel_factor/build_T traffic (~4MB/group) is far below 64MB so C stays L2-resident; the 15-of-16 re-reads convert HBM->L2 (~3x faster). Correctness-identical loop reorder; expect ~1.5-1.7x on the 68% trailing. Edits trailing grid/scheduling only (NOT _CUSTOM_N or n=2048/n=32 routes); profile to confirm L2 hit-rate rises; validate all 3 guards.

Correctness-identical (sfr unchanged). Root cause: fitting C in ~100MB L2 needs group<=100 matrices but panel_factor grid (gb,) needs >=150 (SM count) CTAs for occupancy -- CONTRADICTORY; small groups starve the SMs and panel latency (paid 1x/group) dominates. Reverting to f0d20789.

Brief 3 (L2-cache-blocking by matrix group) -- mechanism REFUTED on this hardware; HEAD unchanged at the global-best base b291fb99 (= f0d20789 content, geomean 4908us / 23.6x, all 3 guards pass, NO regression). EVIDENCE IT FAILS: (1) full-batch benchmark with group=64/16 REGRESSES 2x (n512 9586->18283us, n1024 7538->18079us, geomean 4900->7550). (2) Structured group-size sweep -- n=512 {64:18758,128:12001,160:10670,213:12507,320:9707,640:9669}us; n=1024 {16:18665,30:10854,40:10907,60:7758}us -- shows NO group beats group=B (largest groups merely MATCH baseline; all smaller groups are worse). (3) ncu on group=64: panel_factor Achieved Occupancy = 8.33% (grid (64,) on ~150 SMs). ROOT CAUSE (the brief's premise breaks here): fitting the group's C in the ~100MB L2 requires group<=100 matrices for n=512, but the per-panel kernels' grid is (group,) and need >=150 (the SM count) CTAs for occupancy -- these are CONTRADICTORY, so every L2-fitting group starves the SMs and the panel/build_T/trailing latency (now paid once PER GROUP, 10x for n=512) dominates any trailing L2 win. The consultant's '~1.5-1.7x on the trailing, same bytes moved to L2' ignored that the matrix-group reorder also slashes per-launch parallelism by 10x; the panel_factor in particular is latency/occupancy-bound (worker-1 & I both measured ~15% occ even at full batch) and cannot afford a 10x CTA cut. Note also: keeping the panel batched over all B while grouping only the trailing is IMPOSSIBLE -- the per-matrix dependency panel_j -> trailing_j -> panel_(j+1) forces the panel to be grouped too. CONCLUSION: the trailing DRAM-bytes floor is NOT reachable via L2 matrix-group blocking on sm_120 (150 SMs, ~100MB L2, 1MB/matrix at n=512). This is now confirmed from a 4th independent angle (after nb=64, precision, panel-fusion, C-staging). NEW trailing lever that captures nb=64's traffic win WITHOUT its occupancy collapse: panel-pair-fused trailing for n=512/1024. Keep nb=32 (rank-32 occupancy-friendly footprint), but fuse the FAR-trailing updates of CONSECUTIVE panel pairs over ONE C load: factor panel j (V_j,T_j), eager-update only panel j+1's 32 cols, factor panel j+1 (V_{j+1},T_{j+1}), then update the far trailing (cols >= j+2nb) with BOTH reflectors over a single resident C tile -- read C once, apply rank-32 update for V_j IN PLACE, then rank-32 update for V_{j+1} (reads the just-updated C from SRAM, not DRAM), write C once. Far-trailing C passes 16->8 (halved DRAM) while each tl.dot stays rank-32 (NO [64,BLOCK_N] accumulator = dodges nb=64's collapse; distinct from worker-2's combined-rank-NBO-T which also failed -- here T_j,T_{j+1} stay SEPARATE). MANDATORY: update-2 reads C AFTER update-1 in place (math is H_{j+1}.H_j.C_far, same order as sequential -> identical exact (H,tau)); never compute both V^T C from original C. Validate all 3 guards; profile to confirm trailing DRAM traffic drops. EV ~3-6% global; time-box 2-3 iters.

KEEP: panel-pair-fused trailing for n=512/1024. New trailing_pair3_kernel fuses consecutive panel pairs' far-trailing (cols>=j2+nb): read C, apply H_j1 in place, reduce X2 from updated C', apply H_j2 -- composition H_j2.H_j1.C, identical (H,tau). Far-C reads 4->3/pair, all dots rank-32 (dodges nb=64 occupancy collapse). n=512 ~9550->7790us (1.22x), n=1024 ~7530->7035us (1.06x). Geomean 4055->3681.59us (31.46x, from parent 28.56x). Validates clean incl all 3 guards. fuse_warps=4 key.

MECHANISM (delivered as briefed): new trailing_pair3_kernel fuses consecutive panel PAIRS (j1, j2=j1+nb): far trailing (cols>=j2+nb) gets BOTH reflectors over the far-C tile in 3 row-tiled phases -- phase1 W1=T1^T(V1^T C); phase2 applies H_j1 in place AND reduces X2=V2^T C' from the just-updated C'; phase3 applies H_j2 -- composition H_j2.H_j1.C_far, the SAME order as sequential right-looking, so (H,tau) is bit-identical (verified: sfr 0.005-0.047, all ill-cond + invariance + off-grid guards pass). Panel j1's NARROW trailing updates only panel j2's nb columns; the bulk far trailing is fused. Every tl.dot stays rank-32 (NB x BLOCK_N accumulator) -> never forms the rank-64 tile that collapsed nb=64's occupancy. RESULT: n=512 ~9550->7790us (1.22x!), n=1024 ~7530->7035us (1.06x). The 22% on n=512 EXCEEDED the 3-6% EV -- the fusion saves far-C reads (4->3 per pair, profiler: trailing 77M->pair3 56.6M ns) AND cuts launch count per pair. KEY CONFIG: fuse_warps=4 (sweep-confirmed optimal; fw=8 regresses to ~9100us -- the fused kernel wants moderate occupancy); n=512 (32,32,64,pw4,tw8,fw4), n=1024 (32,32,64,pw8,tw8,fw4).
